evidence: deepseek: "Root at first critical node"; gpt-oss: builds a single adjacency structure and parent traversal; qwen: uses union-find and heap-based graph processing; glm: "Build adjacency list"
affordance_in_statement: The full pool is "minimally sufficient to collapse the variables to a single value" and "omitting any single equation from the full pool would increase the dimension"; together with "m = n - 1", this makes the candidate graph a tree.
removal_suggestion: Replace the guarantee that the entire candidate pool is minimally sufficient and non-redundant with a weaker guarantee that all critical variables are in one connected component. Permit disconnected non-critical components, so a graph with cycles can occur despite m = n - 1.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Treats the candidate equations as a rooted tree and selects the necessary rooted subtree.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The full pool is minimally sufficient and non-redundant, with m = n - 1.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Builds parent/adjacency data for a tree and solves by tree aggregation.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The full pool is minimally sufficient and non-redundant, with m = n - 1.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses graph connectivity/tree-style processing rather than solving the general weighted Steiner-subgraph problem.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The candidate equations form a connected minimally sufficient graph with exactly n - 1 edges.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Builds an adjacency list and relies on the tree structure to determine the required edges.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The full pool collapses all variables and every edge is non-redundant, while m = n - 1.

common_affordance: The minimal connected equation pool with exactly n - 1 edges is a tree, reducing the optimization to selecting the unique terminal-containing subtree.
recommended_edit: Replace the current full-pool minimal-sufficiency and non-redundancy guarantee with: "It is guaranteed only that all critical variables belong to one connected component of the candidate-equation graph; the graph may contain cycles and may have disconnected components containing no critical variable."
